content.user_title: Curate and Apply Layer Reference Sets
content.value_statement: Inconsistent datasets and incompatible models can weaken a trained style while still consuming Creative Units. This skill guides curation, training choices, weight tuning, and contribution checks before generation.
actual_capabilities: Recommend training or an approved reference image based on reuse, subject count, and project scope.
Guide dataset curation for consistent rendering, appropriate variation, clear subjects, and clean images.
Choose among character, object, scene, effect, and general training categories.
Guide reference set weights from 0 to 2 and explain when weight does not apply.
Diagnose degraded reference sets using contribution reports and model compatibility guidance.
Outline training and generation workflows with price estimates, confirmation above 20 Creative Units, and status polling.
limitations: This package provides guidance, not bundled scripts or a standalone training engine.
Execution requires access to Layer tools; detailed training mechanics are delegated to the sibling layer-train-custom-style skill.
Training and generation consume Creative Units and require time; the skill does not guarantee consistent results.
Weight affects LoRA application only and is ignored when sets contribute reference images or prompt text.

use_cases.title: Maintain a studio style
use_cases.description: Select consistent artwork, choose the general category, and plan a reusable reference set for ongoing team generation.

use_cases.title: Build a character library
use_cases.description: Separate subjects into reference sets and vary poses, angles, and expressions while preserving each character design.

use_cases.title: Investigate weak style results
use_cases.description: Review contribution warnings, model selection, and weight settings before spending on another generation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose whether to train
prompt_templates.prompt: I need [asset count] assets for [project duration] using [approved artwork]. Recommend a reference image or trained reference set, and explain the choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: decide whether training is necessary.

prompt_templates.title: Curate a training set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [supplied images] for [subject or style]. Recommend exclusions, useful variation, separate sets, and the appropriate training category. Do not upload anything yet.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a controlled training workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan training for [approved dataset]. Estimate costs before paid actions and request confirmation above 20 Creative Units. Check contributions before generation and report missing tools.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate training and generation with Layer tools.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose degraded style application
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [contribution report] and [run settings] for [reference sets]. Explain degradation, model compatibility, and weight effects. Recommend a revised estimate before any new spend.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: troubleshoot weak or ignored reference sets.

output_examples.input: We have an approved character image and need six images this week. Should we train?
output_examples.output: Use the approved character image as a reference first. Training is not the initial recommendation for this small, short project.

output_examples.input: Our style collection contains twelve consistent pieces and eight pieces with different rendering. We will reuse it for months.
output: Keep the twelve consistent pieces and exclude the eight with different rendering.
Use the general category for an overall aesthetic rather than a single subject.
Estimate training costs before starting and request confirmation above 20 Creative Units.
Estimate generation with automatic model selection and inspect reference set contributions before spending.

output_examples.input: A trained style looks weak with a pinned model, and the estimate reports degradation. Should I raise the weight?
output: Check which reference set degraded and why.
Remove the pinned model or choose a compatible model, then request a new estimate.
Weight changes will not affect a set applied only as reference images or prompt text.
Do not report the trained LoRA as applied when the contribution report indicates otherwise.

best_practices: Curate consistent, clean artwork and vary only the attributes that should change.
Match each set to one subject or style and select its training category deliberately.
Inspect price estimates and contribution reports before spending, and confirm actions above 20 Creative Units.
anti_patterns: Pad a dataset with inconsistent images or mix unrelated subjects into one reference set.
Pin a model without checking reference set compatibility, then treat weak output as a weight problem.
Treat weight as a binary setting or claim a degraded set applied successfully.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for Layer reference set decisions, dataset curation, training categories, weight tuning, and degradation diagnosis.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists all three tools as supported. Executing the workflow still requires access to the relevant Layer tools.

faq.question: When should I train instead of using a reference image?
faq.answer: Train for a look reused over months or a growing subject library. Try an approved reference image for smaller, short projects.

faq.question: Which training category should I choose?
faq.answer: Choose character, object, scene, or effect for that specific intent. Use general for an overall aesthetic across subjects.

faq.question: Does raising weight always strengthen the style?
faq.answer: No. Weight affects LoRA application only. It is ignored when a set contributes reference images or prompt text.

faq.question: Can a degraded run still cost Creative Units?
faq.answer: Yes. A degraded run can succeed and still cost Creative Units. Check contribution reports on the estimate before generation.
